_about: Provenance of every data file in this folder (Atlas v2 2.7.0). Not read by the models; checked by tests/test_provenance.py. Units: energies in hartree unless stated; geometries as stored in the file.

bsse_water_dimer.json.content: (H2O)2: interaction energies without and with counterpoise at R(O...O) = 2.91 A in 11 basis sets; R scan 2.5-4.5 A
bsse_water_dimer.json.method: RHF (conv_tol 1e-10), MP2 and CCSD(T) with frozen O 1s
bsse_water_dimer.json.basis: 6-31G, 6-31G*, 6-31G**, 6-31+G*, 6-31++G**, cc-pVXZ and aug-cc-pVXZ (X = D, T, Q); Pople sets with spherical d (PySCF default)
bsse_water_dimer.json.geometry: rigid monomers r(OH) = 0.9572 A, HOH = 104.52 deg; dimer(R) in the script

casscf_curves.json.content: H2, ethylene twist, N2 dissociation curves
casscf_curves.json.method: RHF, UHF, CASSCF(2,2)/(6,6), NEVPT2, CCSD(T), FCI

cbs_energies.json.content: 9 molecules and their atoms: total energies for basis-set extrapolation and atomisation energies
cbs_energies.json.method: HF, MP2, CCSD, CCSD(T), frozen core; atoms UHF

charges_rhf.json.content: Mulliken, Loewdin and Bader charges, dipole moments (a.u.) and energies of 9 molecules in 4 basis sets
charges_rhf.json.method: RHF (tol 1e-10); Loewdin with each Cartesian d shell orthonormalised first (orientation-independent, 2.7.0); Bader basins on a grid (core.qtaim)
charges_rhf.json.by: recomputed 2026-10-21 (2.7.0); the v1.0 data (script not kept) agree in E (4e-6), Mulliken and dipoles (1e-4), Bader (< 0.007 e); Loewdin changed by the new definition (up to 0.05 e)

ci_cc_h2.json.content: H2/STO-3G: E_g, E_u, K at 73 distances; (H2)n in 6-31G

dft.json.content: E(N) of the H atom, H2+ curves
dft.json.method: the Atlas's own functionals (LSDA, B88, PBE, PW92) on a radial grid and a Becke grid

dispersion.json.content: He2 and (H2O)2: interaction energies, columns [R, HF raw, MP2 raw, HF cp, MP2 cp]; monomer energies [HF, MP2]
dispersion.json.method: RHF (tol 1e-10), all-electron MP2, counterpoise with ghost atoms (Boys-Bernardi)
dispersion.json.basis: He2: aug-cc-pVDZ; (H2O)2: 6-31G* with six Cartesian d
dispersion.json.geometry: He2: R = 4.4-12.0 bohr; (H2O)2: dimer(R) of bsse.py, R(O...O) = 2.40-5.00 A
dispersion.json.program: v1.0: PySCF (script not kept); reproduced with the Atlas v2 engine core.gto
dispersion.json.by: author of the Atlas (v1.0); reproduced 2026-10-21: He2 to 5e-14 Eh (all 77 points), monomers to 3e-10 Eh, (H2O)2 to 1e-11 Eh (14 points checked, R = 2.40-3.05 A)

ladder_methods.json.content: errors relative to FCI (H2O, 6-31G, frozen core); timings (H2O)n/cc-pVDZ; DFT atomisation energies
ladder_methods.json.method: HF, MP2, CISD, CCSD, CCSD(T), FCI; LDA ... B2PLYP, TPSS (xcfun, grid level 5)

mp2_series.json.content: H2/STO-3G by perturbation order; MPn series of water; MP2 share of CCSD(T)
mp2_series.json.method: RHF conv_tol 1e-12, MPn, FCI, CCSD(T); water all electrons

optimization_h2o_pes.json.content: E(r, theta) of symmetric water on a 33 x 33 grid, E[i][j] for r_i, theta_j
optimization_h2o_pes.json.program: v1.0: author (script not kept); reproduced with the Atlas v2 engine core.gto
optimization_h2o_pes.json.by: author of the Atlas (v1.0); reproduced 2026-10-21 to 1e-9 Eh (the rounding of the file)

solvation_cpcm.json.method: B3LYP, C-PCM (PySCF defaults for the cavity)

symmetry_ct.json.method: standard tables (constant CT of the v1.0 pages)
symmetry_ct.json.by: checked by the orthogonality of characters in tests/test_symmetry.py

validation.json.content: geometries of the validation table and of Crawford's water; reference energies of the page
validation.json.method: reference values of the page (Szabo-Ostlund, Crawford); PySCF repeat in tests/fixtures/pyscf/validation_rhf.json
validation.json.by: author of the Atlas; recomputed live by core.validation

vibrations_ct.json.content: character tables used by the normal-mode page
vibrations_ct.json.method: standard tables (constant CT of the v1.0 pages)
vibrations_ct.json.by: same tables as symmetry_ct.json for the groups used; checked through the mode counts in tests/test_vibrations.py
